### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **9** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **16** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `bad7879870200c7cc937d38815d762a3bf5930c7` — the merge of head `4504de0bfb3bcd9188815d1af5b92c6d824e666f` into base `326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin bad7879870200c7cc937d38815d762a3bf5930c7 && git checkout bad7879870200c7cc937d38815d762a3bf5930c7
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d 4504de0bfb3bcd9188815d1af5b92c6d824e666f && git checkout -B drift-repro 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d && git merge --no-ff 4504de0bfb3bcd9188815d1af5b92c6d824e666f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 326453eb9dd5eb72f23c1c5198affd6f177d622d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Scope: .changeset/32246-per-package-loader-storage.md, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/database-loader.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/loader-interface.ts, packages/metadata/src/loaders/memory-loader.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager.ts, packages/metadata/src/metadata-manager-match-endpoint.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/bind-database-loader-row-packages.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/bind-database-loader-row-packages.test.ts, packages/metadata/src/migrations/index.ts, packages/metadata/src/package-slotted-store.ts + read, not reviewed: packages/core/src/package-scoped-resolution.ts (`PackageScopedNameRefusedError`), packages/metadata/src/plugin.ts (the artifact door, the filesystem boot), packages/metadata/src/node-metadata-manager.ts (file-watch drop), packages/metadata-core/src/objects/sys-metadata.object.ts and sys-metadata-history.object.ts (indexes), packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts (router rung `loadDiagnosed('action')`), packages/objectql/src/plugin.ts (`loadMany('action')` resync, `loadManyKeyed('action')` audit), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-catalog-echo.ts (`dropEcho`), scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs, docs/adr/0150 (D3, D4), AGENTS.md (changeset rule)

Green: Build Core, Check Changeset, PR-body guards, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check PR Size, Type Check · source gates, consumer gates and debt ledger, every Lint job, Dogfood Regression Gate, Live E2E UI, Test UI, Plan Test Core shards, Flag docs, filter, Auto Label. The rest are skipped.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `MemoryLoader` keyed by `(package, name)` — right against D4 and ruling Q1. It uses `storeWriteKey` and the registry's own keys, an object-bound action included. Non-slotted types still key by name.
2. `unregisterAt` deleting from `memory:` loaders — right for a removal that names a package, and for `unregisterPackage`. Wrong for a bare removal the registry cannot judge: see ④ M1.
3. `DatabaseLoader` writes `package_id`, and save and delete key by `(package, name)` — right. A package-less body goes into the one holder's row and binds it in the same update. A package's first item takes over the package-less row. Non-slotted paths are behaviourally unchanged.
4. The two-reader split (`loadSlots` / `loadManySlots` beside unscoped `load` / `loadMany` / `loadManyKeyed`) — coherent as a compatibility split, and inside ruling Q1. The router rung and both objectql reads get one item per name, as before. Two caveats are in ④ (S5, S6).
5. History versions per name — right for the ruled case: two holders write versions 1 and 2, pinned. Not right after a removal: see ④ S3.
6. The migration — right. It runs only when an operator calls it. It reads `source = 'database'` rows of the live set. It binds only from the body's own package, leaves `package-less` and `slot-taken` rows, and a second run binds nothing. All pinned.
7. Carried items — 2 (realtime package), 3 (`unregisterPackage` by slot) and 5 (delete by package, `package_id` column pinned) are fixed and pinned. 1, 4 and 6 are recorded in the changeset; 4 is also in `isPackageMember`'s doc, and 6 has a pin. Item 1's record is incomplete: see ④ S4.
8. The #32274 residue pin — flipped. After both packages are removed, the door's `loadSlots`, `list`, bare `get`, `get(…, A)` and `exists` all answer nothing.

### ② Semver level

- Level: `patch` on `@objectstack/metadata` with the BREAKING banner. Correct: `Metadata-protocol: none` takes `patch`, and nothing an author writes moves.
- Declaration lines: `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. There is one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, the same disposition #32069, #32151 and #32198 landed with. Check Changeset is green.
- Published types: the two new `MetadataLoader` members and `MetadataKeyedItem.packageId` are optional, and `MemoryLoader.delete` gains an optional parameter. No implementor breaks. `package-slotted-store.ts` is not exported from the package index. Type Check · workspace is pending.
- FROM → TO completeness: the six declared moves match the diff. Undeclared:
  - **must-fix:** the manager-level move in ④ M1.
  - nit: realtime `created` / `updated` no longer carries a `packageId` that is the `sys_metadata` sentinel or empty, for any type.
  - nit: the endpoint index now sees each package's loader-held `api` item. It is in the prose, with no FROM → TO line.
  - nit: after a removal, the loaders-only reads (`load`, `loadDiagnosed`, `loadMany`, `loadManyKeyed`) also stop answering the door's copy, or answer the other package's. The changeset's "Unchanged" sentence reads as if they never move.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. `unregister('action', name, { packageId })` leaves an object-bound action's registry slot — confirmed. `storeRemovalKeys` with a package returns only the object-less key. On `main` the row was already deleted; this PR also deletes the door's copy. So `get` and `list` still serve the action from the registry, while the router rung and objectql's `loadMany('action')` no longer see it. Callers: 0. Escalated to the seat: it has no carrier and needs a card. The same card should cover a bare removal of a bound name two packages hold, which is not refused, because the holder count reads only the object-less key.
2. The per-package view behind optional `loadSlots` / `loadManySlots` — answered in ① 4. It keeps the ruled non-narrowing of `action`'s readers.
3. The migration is operator-run, not run at schema time — accepted. The card asks only for re-runnable and never guessing. Reads are right without it, and a save binds its own row; both pinned.
4. Downstream suites ran at `52729d39` — accepted. The delta to this head is two files, the changeset wording and the migration test's row store.
5. The `Skills-docs` line and the PR-subscription posture — not contract matters.
6. Out-of-scope items: the non-slotted door residue (ruling Q4) and rollback by package are the seat's to file. See ④ S1 for the rollback wording.
7. For #32162: once `permission` joins the set, `dropEcho`'s bare `metadata.unregister` becomes a first-party removal that reaches the door's store. That is new with this PR, and it is where M1 becomes reachable.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes the D3 refusal real at the loaders and takes no declared capability away. One defect blocks.

**M1, must-fix — a bare removal of a name two packages hold in the loaders is swallowed and announced as done.**
- State: an empty registry over rows, or a cluster peer after replay, with two packages' items stored.
- `unregister(type, name)` judges holders from the registry alone, so it finds none.
- The storage loop then calls `loader.delete(type, name)`. Both loaders now throw `PackageScopedNameRefusedError` there.
- `unregisterAt` catches it and hands it to `reportMetaItemDeleteFailure`, which logs at `error` and tells the operator to check the datasource connection.
- Nothing is deleted. The call resolves, `bulkUnregister` counts it as succeeded, and the realtime and watcher `deleted` events go out.
- In the same state `get(type, name)` refuses `409` naming both holders, so reads and removal disagree about who holds the name.
- The `409` code and status never reach the caller (ADR-0112). `unregisterAt`'s own doc says a refused removal announces nothing.
- The move is undeclared at the manager: the changeset declares only `DatabaseLoader.delete` as refused. The same call sequence on `main` deleted the row.
- With two loaders the outcome can be half-applied: one deletes, the other refuses.
- First-party reach today is 0; it becomes reachable with #32162.
- Fix: for a slotted type removed with no package, judge holders over the registry and the loaders' slots before the storage loop, or rethrow the refusal before anything is touched. Add a live-set pin on a peer manager and a FROM → TO line.

Should-fix:
- **S1** — rollback can put one package's body in the other's row. `registerRollback` updates the first row of `(type, name)`. With versions now numbered per name, rolling back to P1's version can overwrite P2's bound row. This mode is new with per-package rows. It is ruled a follow-up, but the changeset says only that rolling back one package's row is a follow-up. Say what happens, and file the card before landing.
- **S2** — `get` and `list` disagree when the registry holds one package's slot and a loader holds another's. `list` now adds the loader's item, pinned. `get(type, name, thatPackage)` returns `undefined`, because a `settled` registry answer never asks the loaders. Bare `get` resolves to the registry's holder, where an empty registry would refuse.
- **S3** — the next version is read from live rows, not from history. With P1 at v1 and P2 at v2, removing P2 and saving it again reuses v2. The history insert collides and is dropped with a console error. `main` has the same class on delete and recreate. The history schema's own rule is the maximum over history.
- **S4** — carried item 1 is recorded as "only a slot no loader holds is lost". It omits that a removal on one node leaves each peer's door copy, which then serves the removed package's item. Add it to the record.
- **S5** — `DatabaseLoader`'s "saved last" is really "changed last". An identical re-save is skipped with no version bump, so `load` can answer a different package than the door does, and than `main` did.
- **S6** — `DatabaseLoader.loadSlots` is a type-wide read filtered in memory. A `get` miss on a slotted type costs a full type scan when the type cache is cold; it was one `findOne`.

Nits:
- The PR body says the refusal pin asserts `code`. It asserts the class, `status`, reason and candidates.
- The two new `database-loader.test.ts` cases use a fixed `agent`.
- The manager-level pins use only the `_packageId` shape. The envelope shape is pinned at the migration and the loader.
- `stat` reads an arbitrary row of a two-row name.
- The migration reads through the raw driver, so it does not skip legacy-organization rows as the loader does.
- `loadMany` order moves for unnamed rows and for a bare slot taken over.
- The registry and `DatabaseLoader` each judge a package-less write from their own holders, so they can pick different slots when their holder sets differ.

Break attempts:
- Two holders, then save, read: held and pinned over three loader combinations.
- Remove by package, and remove the last holder: held.
- Bare remove on an empty registry: broken, M1.
- Envelope item vs `_packageId`-only item: both attribute through `storedItemPackageId`.
- A package-less row beside package rows: own row, bare read refused, removable once both packages are gone, as recorded.
- Non-slotted CONTROL: unchanged in both loaders and the manager.
- History rollback for a two-holder name: S1.
- Concurrent saves of two packages: both rows can take the same version and the second history row is dropped. The path is non-transactional, as on `main`.
- A cluster peer after replay: reads are right; removal is S4.
- `code` / `status`: right on reads, lost in M1.
- The pins iterate the live set: yes, with a not-empty floor, an `action` case behind `runIf`, and the realtime leg keyed on the live event enum.
